liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dark Star** (4 reviews, 1 other source): Reviewer ranks this Dark Star among the best ever, with Phil's bass thundering at key points; Reviewer finds the Dark Star into Dew gorgeous [4][6][7][12][17]
- **Morning Dew** (1 review, 1 other source): The Feelin' Groovy jam leading into Dew is called remarkable; A very fast Feelin' Groovy jam comes near the end of the Dark Star [4][6]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 review): This source picks up mid-jam; the portion present is extremely hot, with an intense eighth minute resembling a 1972 Dark Star [16]
- Reviewer says Jerry is wailing throughout the show [11]
- Blogger calls this their favorite Dead version of the song, praising Donna's singing and Keith's piano [20]

## The recordings

- **gd72-11-13.aud.vernon.17416.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 22 songs; 201 min; rated 2.33/5 by 3 [1]. Said about its sound: Notes say it is almost complete apart from tape flips and mainly suits completists and audience tape collectors [1]
- **gd1972-11-13.159120.aud.ryan.welch.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 22 songs; 179 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd72-11-13.aud.hanno.10089.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 175 min; rated 3.39/5 by 18 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is called fairly decent for 1972 and better than some other audience tapes, such as 4/7/72; Most of the show was recorded by Bear and sounds very listenable, better than many 1980s audience tapes [7][12]
- **gd1972-11-13.aud.cotsman.7518.sbefail.shnf**: audience recording; 8 songs; 88 min; rated 4.4/5 by 5 [4]. Said about its sound: Tape begins partway into Playin', probably missing only a minute or two; Excellent for 1972 audience tape, deep and clear, but missing most of set one and all of Playin'; Very good audience recording for the era; first set missing except Playin'; one splice in Dark Star at 11:20 [4][16][17]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says Kansas City is their hometown [6]
- The Dead visited Kansas City only once in the early 1970s; locals were starstruck and unfamiliar with the culture [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd72-11-13.aud.vernon.17416.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Kevin Well and Matt Vernon; source: AUD(unknown mics) > C(x3) > Nak > Fostex D5 A/D @ 44.1 > CD [1]
- **gd1972-11-13.159120.aud.ryan.welch.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Karl Ryan; transferred by Tim Welch;Charlie Miller;Scott Clugston; source: Karl Ryan's Master Audience Reels (unknown mics/deck); Tim Welch's 1st generation cassettes > DAT (16/48kHz) [2]
- **gd72-11-13.aud.hanno.10089.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Hanno; source: Audience Recording [3]. Also: Notes credit Bear with recording the portion from Playin' through Casey Jones [12]
- **gd1972-11-13.aud.cotsman.7518.sbefail.shnf**: transferred by Jeff Cotsman; source: AUD>MR>C>D>CD>EAC>SHN [4]
